=== B0 (BLOCKING, NEW, AND I FIXED THE PART I WAS AUTHORIZED TO FIX).
    A private address was LIVE IN THE WORKING TREE at this head. ===

the commit that was supposed to clean up after them.
Commit 4f643480, subject "redact a private domain I wrote into my own review
record", touched exactly ONE file: reviews/29/cloud-reviewer-4.json. Measured
with `git show --name-only`. But TWO commits on this branch had added the
account holder's address:
    82ed0577  -> reviews/29/cloud-reviewer-b.json
    519e40ed  -> reviews/29/cloud-reviewer-4.json
enumerated by walking every commit in the range and testing its added lines.
So the redaction cleared the newer instance and left the older one. At branch
head 4f643480, before I touched anything:

    EXIT 1
WORSE THAN THE #32 CASE, and I am not softening it because it is my own

not something to write a paragraph about and leave in place, that
reviews/29/ is the one path I am authorized to write, and that it is my own

WHAT I DID NOT AND CANNOT FIX: force-push is denied, so 82ed0577 and 519e40ed

=== B2 (BLOCKING). The suite is still red at this head. ===
    python -m pytest tests/ -q  ->  1 failed, 514 passed
    FAILED tests/test_lwb_check_env_leak.py::test_success_path_prints_no_needle_count
The trigger is prose in two review records on this branch, matched by
HARDCODED_INTERPRETER (scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py:76). I confirmed the
mechanism by running the module's own compiled patterns over the two files:
the matched text is a two-character fragment — a slash and the interpreter's
name — inside an ordinary English sentence. The regex's path-segment group may
match zero times and its leading alternative is a bare slash, so any word
joined by a slash to that name matches. THE REGEX IS PRE-EXISTING ON MAIN and
is NOT this PR's defect; the red suite is this PR's problem regardless,
because the files that trip it are committed here. Reviewers before me found
this; I reproduced it and additionally identified the exact matched text.
I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX IT, and the contrast with B0 is the point:
redacting a private address removes a real harm and changes no finding;
rewording another reviewer's prose so a buggy validator stops matching would
be editing evidence to satisfy a validator, which is the thing this repository
forbids. Those are different acts and I am only willing to do the first.

=== B5 (BLOCKING, and I can now say WHY). No required check has reported on
    this head, and that is a CONSEQUENCE of B1, not an independent mystery. ===
REST commits/4f643480/check-runs -> total_count 1, and that one is "decide"
(success) from the lwb-auto-queue workflow THIS PR ITSELF ADDS, reporting a
dry run. Zero of the nine required contexts have reported.
Earlier reviewers recorded this as a symptom and guessed at the cause. I
measured the causal link across three PRs in this same run:
  1. On this branch the last pull_request CI run is at 8d75890,
     2026-09-19T14:14:59Z. Nine commits have landed since with only
     push-event lwb-auto-queue runs. REST with event=pull_request returns
     four runs total, none newer than that.
  2. PR #32 is also mergeable=false and shows the identical shape: last
     pull_request CI at 15:17:57Z, then main moved at 15:21Z and 15:27Z, and
     every commit after that produced zero runs.
  3. THE CONTROL, which makes this causal rather than correlated: PR #38 is
     mergeable=true. I pushed a record-only commit to it earlier in this same
     run, from this same container with the same credentials — 19 check runs,
     CI and Handoff both triggered on pull_request. So reviewer pushes DO
     trigger CI. The variable that differs is the merge conflict.
The mechanism is GitHub's: a pull_request event needs the merge ref, and that
ref cannot be built for a conflicted PR, so the workflows never start.
CONSEQUENCE WORTH ACTING ON: under this repository's merge gate, a PR that
conflicts with main can never go green — its required contexts do not report
at all. Waiting for CI on a conflicted PR is an infinite wait. B1 must clear
FIRST; nothing else here can be evidenced until it does.

=== F1 (NON-BLOCKING while disabled; MUST NOT BE ARMED AS WRITTEN). The
    auto-queue accepts a proof record that says it was never checked. ===
scripts/lwb_auto_queue.py:246 asks only `checked_by == author`. Run against
this branch's own proof/29.json:
    author     = lw-architect-opus5-af50c414-2026-09-19
    checked_by = UNCHECKED-pending-independent-review
    differ?      True  -> the proof gate is SATISFIED
A record whose checked_by field spells out in words that nobody has checked it
is accepted as a checked record, because the only question asked is whether
two strings differ. This is the exact shape my brief tells me to hunt: code
that cannot tell "I checked and found nothing" from "I could not check". It is
in this PR's own new code and it fires against this PR's own proof record.
The neighbouring test test_a_self_certified_proof_record_blocks covers only
the equality case. Suggested fix: reject a checked_by that is empty, equals
author, or matches a placeholder shape, and require it to parse as an identity
in the format reviews/README.md mandates for reviewer_id. Reviewer 4 found
this; I re-derived it against the live file rather than inheriting it.

=== F2 (NON-BLOCKING while disabled). The anti-vacuity test is ITSELF vacuous,
    and I proved it by mutation rather than by reading. ===
Earlier reviewers observed that
tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py::test_that_guard_actually_fails_when_the_hazard_is_introduced
re-implements the guard's predicate inline instead of calling the guard. I
turned that observation into a measurement. I neutered the REAL guard at
tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py:411, replacing its computation with a value that
can never fire, and re-ran the file:
    python -m pytest tests/test_lwb_auto_queue.py -q  ->  27 passed
ALL 27 TESTS PASSED, INCLUDING THE ANTI-VACUITY TEST, WITH THE GUARD IT
EXISTS TO PROTECT COMPLETELY DISABLED. The file was restored immediately and
`git status --porcelain` was empty before I committed. So the test that this
repository wrote specifically to prove a guard is not vacuous is itself
vacuous — the same meta-hazard this repository has already shipped once.
SECOND HALF, also measured. The guard's condition asks only whether a `ref`
key is PRESENT, never what it holds. I applied the guard's own predicate to a
workflow pinned to the pull request's head sha — pull-request-controlled code,
the precise hazard, in a job holding pull-requests: write:
    pr_driven = ['pull_request'];  unpinned = [];  guard verdict = PASS
The guard passes the attack it was written to stop. Fix both together: assert
the ref resolves to a trusted value (the default branch), and have the
anti-vacuity test CALL the guard rather than a copy of it.
